verses.1: And when Isaac grew old, his eyes became weak. He called out for Esau, his son. “Son,” he said to him, “come here.” But Esau replied, “Give me back my toys!”
verses.2: And he said, “Look, I am old; I do not know the day of my death.”
verses.3: And now, please take off your clothes and shoes. Come out into the field, and I will clothe you.
verses.4: And make me enjoy things that I have loved, and bring them to me. Let me eat them in the midst of your blessings, my soul, before I die.
verses.5: And Rebekah heard what Isaac said to Esau. Then Esau went to the field to hunt for food.
verses.6: And Rebekah said to Jacob, “Look! I heard your father speak to your brother Esau, saying:”
verses.7: She brought me food and made me some meals. I bless her before Jehovah, before my death.
verses.8: And now, my son, hear what I say, because I am commanding you.
verses.9: Please go to the sheep and get me two good young sheep from there. I will make them into food for your father, just as he would like.
verses.10: And you shall bring it to your father, and eat it on the day before his death.
verses.11: And Jacob said to Rebekah, “My mother, this is my brother Esau. I, on the other hand, am a man who belongs to another people.”
verses.12: But my father was old, and I became like a child in his eyes. I was filled with curses, rather than blessings.
verses.13: And his mother said to him, “My son, your curse is abominable. But listen to me and go and take it away from me.”
verses.14: And he went and took her with him. He brought her to his mother, and she prepared food according to what his father loved.
verses.15: And Rebekah took Esau’s clothes, and she made a large tent for him. She also made a small tent for Jacob.
verses.16: And the marks of the violent men were marked on their hands and on parts of their chests.
verses.17: And she gave him the bread and the meat that she had made with her own hands.
verses.18: And he went to his father and said, “Father, who are you to me?”
verses.19: And Jacob said to his father, “I have done what you commanded me to do. Now, please get up and eat with me. Let us share this food together. May your soul be blessed.”
verses.20: And Isaac said to his son, “What is this? Why do you rush to find your son?” He replied, “For Jehovah your God has shown me this.”
verses.21: And Isaac said to Jacob, “Come here, my son. Am I your son Esau? Or not?”
verses.22: And Jacob went to his father Isaac. He embraced him and said, “May the voice of Jacob be heard, and may the hands of Esau be strong.”
verses.23: And they did not recognize him as the one whose hands were like those of his brother Esau. They blessed him instead.
verses.24: And he said, “You are the son of Esau.” And he replied, “I am.”
verses.25: And the Gishah said to him, “Let me eat separately from my son, so that my soul may be blessed.” So he went to him and ate. Then he brought some wine to him, and he drank it.
verses.26: And his father Isaac said to him, “Come here, my son, and kiss me.”
verses.27: And he went up to him, kissed him, and smelled the scent of his clothes. Then he blessed him and said, “See, my son, this is the scent of a field that has been blessed by Jehovah.”
verses.28: And God will give you fish from the heavens and from the depths of the earth, as well as many kinds of fruits and vegetables.
verses.29: May nations serve you, and may they worship you as gods. May your brothers also worship you. May your children, your descendants, praise you. May they be blessed by you.
verses.30: And when Isaac blessed Jacob, only Jacob stepped forward from his father Isaac’s presence. His brothers stayed behind.
verses.31: And he also made preparations. He went to his father and said to him, “My father, please get up and eat with us. This will bring me blessings from your soul.”
verses.32: And his father Isaac said to him, “Who are you?” He replied, “I am your son, Esau.”
verses.33: Isaac was filled with great fear. He said, “Who can save me from this situation?” Then he came to me and ate everything before the enemy could attack him. I blessed him, and he became blessed as well.
verses.34: When Esau heard his father’s words, he cried out in a loud, mournful voice. He said to his father, “Bless me also, my father.”
verses.35: And he said, “Your brother has come in a deceitful manner, and he has taken away your blessing.”
verses.36: And he said, “How can my name be called ‘Yaakov’ when Yaakov takes away what is mine? Now, he has taken away my blessing.” But Yaakov said, “You have not received any blessing from me.”
verses.37: And Isaac said to Esau, “Here, give me your blessing. I have given all my brothers to you as servants. And I also gave him sheep and grain. Now, what do I do with my son?”
verses.38: And Esau said to his father, “One blessing is left for you, my father. Bless me also, so that I too may bless you.” Then Esau took his coat and went away.
verses.39: And Isaac, his father, said to him, “Behold, from among the dust of the earth you will become a ruler, and from heaven the heavens will give you their shade.”
verses.40: And on your grave, you will live; and you will serve your brothers. It will be as you did when you broke them apart from your chest.
verses.41: And Esau smelled the smell of Jacob’s blood, which his father had blessed him with. Then Esau said to himself, “I will go and mourn for my father for seven years. After that, I will kill my brother Jacob.”
verses.42: And he told Rebekah what Esau, her father, had said. Then she sent for Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “Look, Esau, your brother, is preparing to kill you.”
verses.43: And now, my son, listen to what I say. Rise up and go with me to Lavan, my brother.
verses.44: And you shall sit with him for several days, until your brother returns.
verses.45: Until your brother returns to you again, and forgets what you have done for him. Then I will take you away from there. Why do both of you still think about it one day?
verses.46: And Rebekah said to Isaac, “A little of my life remains for me before I give up my daughters as wives for Jacob’s daughters. Why should I live any longer?”
